brief.what: The COP31 international climate summit, which took place in Turkey, has officially concluded without reaching a deal. Negotiators from around the world were unable to produce a final agreement after failing to find common ground on the issue of fossil fuels.
brief.who: The main actors involved were international negotiators and government representatives from various countries who participated in the climate talks in Turkey.
brief.context: These talks represent a global effort to address the ongoing climate crisis. The article notes that fossil fuels are considered the primary driver of climate change, which placed them at the center of the negotiations.
brief.why: According to the report, the summit ended in disappointment because countries could not reach an agreement regarding fossil fuels. The failure to bridge these differences prevented the adoption of a final deal.

also.title: Amazon warns NYC of $5 fees due to mayor’s delivery bill; Mamdani cries ‘greed’
also.note: Fox Business includes a direct quote from Mamdani calling the move 'greed' and explicitly attributes the bill to the mayor.

brief.what: Amazon has initiated a campaign urging its New York City customers to oppose a new delivery bill backed by Zohran Mamdani. The company is warning online shoppers via pop-up notifications that they could face a $5 fee per order if the proposed legislation is enacted. This direct appeal to the consumer base serves as a tactic to pressure local lawmakers by highlighting potential costs to the public.
brief.who: The main actors include Amazon, which is actively lobbying its customers; Zohran Mamdani, the legislator supporting the bill; and New York City's City Hall, which is currently in a legislative battle with the company.
brief.context: This move represents a significant escalation in the friction between the e-commerce giant and New York City officials over delivery-related regulations and municipal oversight.
brief.why: Amazon warns that the $5 fee is a necessary response to the proposed legislation, while Mamdani has countered by describing the company's warning as an act of greed.

items.title: Forint Jumps After Hungary Softens Interest-Rate Guidance
items.author: Zoltan Simon and Thomas Escritt
items.summary: The Hungarian forint rose after the central bank indicated it has less room to cut interest rates. The policy shift follows a recent market selloff.

brief.what: The Hungarian forint jumped in value after the country's central bank softened its monetary policy guidance. This shift indicates that the central bank sees more limited room to cut interest rates following a recent market selloff.
brief.who: The primary actor is the Hungarian central bank, which is responsible for setting the nation's monetary policy and issuing guidance to the markets. The movement of the forint reflects the reaction of currency traders and investors to this news.
brief.context: The central bank's decision comes in the wake of a market selloff that has influenced the economic environment. Monetary policy guidance is a key tool used by central banks to manage market expectations regarding future interest rate adjustments.
brief.why: The central bank adjusted its stance because it determined that the capacity for further interest rate reductions has diminished. This assessment was made citing the impact of the recent market selloff on the available room for policy maneuvers.
